# Including phylogenetic uncertainty - Julia verision

Often, we do not have a single phylogeny but a set of phylogenies, e.g., from a Bayesian phylogenetic inference. When using phylogenetic control, we want to marginalize over the phylogenetic uncertainty. Doing this in R + Stan is possible but cumbersome and computationallly expensive. Therefore I will explores re-implementations of the R/Stan models in Juilia + Turing.jl, and in Python + NumPyro.

Let's start with Julia.

## Data

Now we will use the 902 posterior samples of the EDGE tree.
```{julia}
# Create data directory if it doesn't exist
isdir("../data") || mkpath("../data")

# Paths
tgz_url = "https://github.com/rbouckaert/global-language-tree-pipeline/releases/download/v1.0.0/all_trees.tgz"
tgz_file = "../data/all_trees.tgz"
tar_file = "../data/all_trees.tar"
tree_dir = "../data/all_trees/"

# Download and extract
if !isdir(tree_dir)
    Downloads.download(tgz_url, tgz_file)

    # Decompress .tgz to .tar
    open(tgz_file) do f_in
        open(tar_file, "w") do f_out
            write(f_out, transcode(GzipDecompressor, read(f_in)))
        end
    end

    # Extract .tar archive
    Tar.extract(tar_file, tree_dir)
    # Move all files from ../data/all_trees/all_trees to ../data/all_trees
    inner_dir = joinpath(tree_dir, "all_trees")
    if isdir(inner_dir)
        for f in readdir(inner_dir; join=true)
            mv(f, joinpath(tree_dir, basename(f)); force=true)
        end
        rm(inner_dir; force=true, recursive=true)
    end
    # Clean up
    rm(tgz_file)
    rm(tar_file)
end


# Load all Newick trees
tree_files = glob("*.tree", tree_dir)

trees = [parsenewick(read(f, String)) for f in tree_files]

# Optionally strip suffixes
for tree in trees
    for tip in getleaves(tree)
        tip.name = split(tip.name, "_")[1]
    end
end

```


## Grambank data

We use the same sample as in the previous notebook

```{julia}
#| vscode: {languageId: julia}

d = CSV.File("../data/grambank_vals_pruned.csv") |> DataFrame
taxa = sort(unique(d.Language_ID))
```


Now we prune the trees to only include the languages in the data.

```{julia}
#| vscode: {languageId: julia}
pruned_trees = [deepcopy(t) for t in trees]
for t in pruned_trees
    droptips!(t, setdiff(getleafnames(t), taxa))
end
```


## Vanilla regression

We will use the same model as in the previous notebook, but now we will use Turing.jl to implement it.

The likelihood is implemented as a Turing model like this:

```{julia}
#| vscode: {languageId: julia}
@model function vanilla_regression(x, y)
    N = length(y)
    
    # Center x
    means_x = mean(x)
    Xc = x .- means_x

    # Priors
    alpha ~ LocationScale(0, 2.5, TDist(3))
    beta ~ Normal(0, 2)

    # Likelihood
    for i in 1:N
        y[i] ~ BernoulliLogit(alpha + beta * Xc[i])
    end
end
```

The `generated quantities` block from the Stan model is implemented as a separate function:

```{julia}
#| vscode: {languageId: julia}
#| 
# Log-likelihood, posterior predictive, and prior predictive in a function:
function generated_quantities(chain, x, y)
    N = length(y)
    means_x = mean(x)
    Xc = x .- means_x

    nsamples = length(chain[:alpha])
    loglik = zeros(nsamples, N)
    y_rep = zeros(Int, nsamples, N)
    y_prior = zeros(Int, nsamples, N)

    for s in 1:nsamples
        α = chain[:alpha][s]
        β = chain[:beta][s]

        for n in 1:N
            # log-likelihood
            loglik[s, n] = logpdf(BernoulliLogit(α + β * x[n]), y[n])

            # posterior predictive
            y_rep[s, n] = rand(BernoulliLogit(α + β * Xc[n]))

            # prior predictive
            αp = rand(LocationScale(0, 2.5, TDist(3)))
            βp = rand(Normal(0, 2))
            y_prior[s, n] = rand(BernoulliLogit(αp + βp * Xc[n]))
        end
    end

    return (loglik = loglik, y_rep = y_rep, y_prior = y_prior)
end
```

Let's run the model:

```{julia}
#| vscode: {languageId: julia}

# Run the model
@time begin
    model = vanilla_regression(d.x, d.y)
    chain = sample(
        model, 
        NUTS(), 
        MCMCThreads(),
        2_000,
        4,
        discard_initial = 1000,
        progress = true,
        )

end
# Print summary of the chain
describe(chain)
```

The 95% credible intervals for the parameters are:

```{julia}
#| vscode: {languageId: julia}

hpd(chain)
```


```{julia}
#| vscode: {languageId: julia}
# plot the posterior distributions of alpha and beta

plot(chain, [:alpha, :beta]; legend=:topright, title="Posterior distributions of alpha and beta")

```
